validation.initial_failure: The legacy descriptor fixture tried to replace literal {bx} in a current {ax} constraint and threw before calling the renderer. Original failing reports are retained. The repaired fixture independently constructs generic and fixed-BX historical contracts and checks 24 mode/segment/result combinations.

validation.post_integration_scope: All listed targets run fully except NeverDX86VirtualizationSourceTests, filtered to X86DescriptorStateSource.* and EveryOwnedInstructionSurvivesBothSourceRoutes. The original 367-case reports remain tied to their earlier frozen source; they are not claimed as a fully passing final-source run.
validation.red_diagnostics: Retained role-red and source-bits-red reports show the original pointer-parameter promotion and actual UBSan high-bit process-address failure. The final tests retain an explicit integer-width invariant and execute an ordinary DS load beside the physical input.

limitations: No SKINIT instruction is executed or emulated. Native boundary oracles stop before the independently decoded 0f 01 de; source executions replace launch with a recorder.
CPU reset, TPM attestation, successful launch, physical SLB accesses, native privilege/feature/fault ordering and launch-time atomicity are unqualified.
The compatibility SDK has no native llvm.x86.skinit API and uses the owned real-instruction fallback. The native SDK checks the new intrinsic as well.
NeverC frontend supports x64 targets; i386 qualification uses LLVM and the existing C compiler.
Skipped tests are included with their exact reasons. Optional NeverC tests in the original broad suite were not configured; AMX hardware is unavailable on this host.

VMRUN, full machine-state continuations, AMX stack-row addressing, unowned/i386 x87-MMX-3DNow, MPX and the other documented global gaps remain open. No final LLVM release, SDK pin or gitlink update is claimed.
